full_judgment:
3. The petitioner hereof as plaintiff filed the suit for declaration and injunction to the effect that the order dated 31.03.1986 passed by the defendant No. 4, U. R. O. Chittalmari Upazilla, in Miscellaneous Review Case No. 100 /84-85 in respect of settlement of the 'Ka' schedule land is illegal, void and without jurisdiction and is not binding on the plaintiff and to restrain the defendant No.1-3 from entering   into the said 'Ka' schedule land of the p. plaint forcibly and not to dispossess the plaintiff therefrom, by granting permanent injunction; and also prayed for a temporary injunction to that effect pending disposal of the suit contending, amongst others that the suit land belonged to one Nironjan and that on his death as well as on the death of his son Nityanondo, kanaklata, being the wife of Nironjan an mother of Nityanondo, inherited the life long-interest on the case land and to meet the funeral and others expenses she sold the same to the plaintiff by executing and registering a sale deed dated 30.09.1985 and accordingly got possession thereon and thus the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the suit land, detailed as schedule 'Ka' of the plaint, and while thus owning and possessing the said land and enjoying usufructs therefrom the plaintiff came to know that the defendant No. 3 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 0896 / 81-82 in the office of U. R. O., the respondent No 4 hereof, by submitting copy of a deed of gift dated 23.04.1976 claiming to have been made by Nironjan and got mutated his name in the records of right and that there-against the said kanaklata filed review case No. 100/ 84-85 under Section 150 of the State acquisition and Tenancy Act and that the plaintiff got himself added as a party in the said proceeding and thereafter the plaintiff filed a criminal case asserting that the aforesaid gift deed is a forged document, being Complaint Case No. 153 of 1985, pending in the Court of A. D. M. and that the said defendant No. 3 having failed to produce the original deed gift, though called for, the defendant No. 4 was required to investigate into matter and the said defendant No. 4 illegally and against the provision of law, in the absence of the said deed gift in favour of the defendant No. 3 as successor-in-interest, passed an illegal order in favour of the defendant No. 3 and that being aggrieved there-against the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Appeal Case No. 29 of 1986 and obtained an order staying the operation of the impugned order. Thereafter, the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on 15.03.1987 threatened to dispossess the plaintiff forcibly from the suit land and hence the suit. 

 4. The defendant No. 1-3 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, amongst others, that kanaklata, vendor of the plaintiff, did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land and she left for India during the lifetime of her husband Nironjan and she was staying in India having married there and that Nironjan had no son named Nityanondo and that the sale deed dated 30.09.1985 is a forged deed without consideration and void and that said kanaklata herself did not file any review case in the office of the U. R. O. Chittalmari, and that the plaintiff filed Criminal Case to harass the defendants and that the plaintiff having lost in Miscellaneous Review Case No. 100/ 84-85 has filed the instant suit knowing well that he has no ground for any success. The defendant No.3 inherited the property of Nironjan, being his mother, as per Hindu Daybhaga law of inheritance, and she is in possession accordingly and that the plaintiff has no right, title and interest or possession in the suit land and hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 " From the order dated 29.10.2001 in Appeal Case No. 168 of 1997, it appears that the prayer (Ka) is under challenge which is admitted and supported by the certified copy of the order dated 29.10.2001 in Appeal No. 168 of 1997. The certified copy is submitted by the learned advocate for the petitioners today in this court, is kept on record of this court. Hence the prayer of the suit so far it related to the R.O.R. is concerned and for the determination of R.O.R. and the status of the plaintiff and having no prayer for declaration of title to the effect and thus the suit was not maintainable in law. This court is of the view that the plaintiff having already had recourse to the procedure provided under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the higher authority, i. e. the Assistant Commissioner of Land, Bagerhat earlier set aside the said impugned prayer of the suit, should not be allowed after being unsuccessfully therein to have the R.O.R in his name to adopt the present petitioner by way of suit in a Civil court."
